events.title: Growing resilience through community-led permagardens in Somalia: How women farmers are improving nutrition, food security and livelihoods with climate-smart agriculture
events.summary: Country: Somalia Source: Concern Worldwide Building resilient food systems at community level remains a priority across many of the contexts where Concern works. Yet establishing productive and sustainable gardens can be challenging, particularly in areas affected by climate shocks, water scarcity and limited access to agricultural inputs. In Somalia, Concern and its partner Lifeline Gedo have been addressing these challenges through the Irish Aid-funded Preventing Wasting in Madera Triangle (PWIMT) programme . Working through Mother-to-Mother Groups in the Gedo region, women farmers received training and technical support to improve soil fertility, manage water resources and grow diverse, nutritious crops using locally available materials and resources. Through community permagardens, participants applied climate-smart and agroecological farming practices to increase food production and diversify household diets. What is a permagarden and why does it matter? A permagarden is more than a vegetable garden. Drawing on principles of permaculture and bio-intensive agriculture, it is designed to maximise food production on small plots of land while making sustainable use of natural resources. Through techniques that improve soil health, conserve water and promote crop diversity, permagardens enable households to produce nutritious food that is available from production in the permagardens or accessible in markets from sale of surpluses throughout the year.
